question: A 57-year-old man presents with a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months as shown in the picture. He has had chronically swollen legs for over 10 years. His mother and brother had similar problems with their legs. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years earlier, but has no other past medical history. He has a blood pressure of 126/84 and heart rate of 62/min. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
analysis: The patient's symptoms and history are most consistent with chronic venous insufficiency. The presence of a large wound on the lower leg that has been present for 6 months, along with a history of chronically swollen legs and a previous DVT, strongly suggests venous insufficiency. The family history of similar leg problems also supports this diagnosis. Arterial ulcers typically occur on the toes or feet and are associated with peripheral artery disease, which is not indicated here. Marjolin ulcer is a malignant transformation of a chronic wound, which is less likely given the information. Lymphedema would cause swelling but not typically ulceration. Kaposi sarcoma is a vascular tumor associated with immunosuppression, which is not suggested in this case.
